what: The voice reference. Not a stimulus — nothing in out/ is derived from it.

clip.transcript:
[S1] Did you end up going to that new café near campus?
[S2] Yeah, I went yesterday after class. It was actually pretty nice.
clip.role: identifies both voices, and documents which tag is which dataset speaker

speakers.line: Did you end up going to that new café near campus?
Yeah, I went yesterday after class. It was actually pretty nice.

mapping_warning: S1 and S2 run opposite to the dataset's A and B. S1 is aKw9UnnjRq5scbeeGI7Z, which make_audio.py assigns to speaker B; S2 is s3TPKV1kjDlVtZbl4Ksh, which it assigns to speaker A. Wiring a cloning renderer S1->A and S2->B would swap the voices against the ElevenLabs renders, and every metric splits by renderer, so the difference would look like a renderer effect.

voice_match_reference.role: the timbre a generated vocalization clip has to match, for a verifier to compare against
voice_match_reference.used_by: an audio model checking that a Dia-generated gasp or groan sounds like the same person as the ElevenLabs speech it will be spliced into
voice_match_reference.why_no_transcript: None is needed. A verifier comparing timbre does not read words, so this is not a cloning input and the transcript gap that applies to one does not apply here.
voice_match_reference.why_speaker_a: A produces every vocalization — the turns run A-B-A-B-A, so the sound always falls in turn 5, which is A's. Speaker B never makes one, so B's voice never has to be matched.

clone_source.voice: one voice throughout — dataset speaker A, s3TPKV1kjDlVtZbl4Ksh
clone_source.transcript:
[S1] Yeah, I went yesterday after class. It was actually pretty nice.
[S2] We had a cup of coffee and chat a lot about what recently happened.

lines.text: Yeah, I went yesterday after class. It was actually pretty nice.
We had a cup of coffee and chat a lot about what recently happened.

clone_source.why_a_single_voice: Dia only ever produces speaker A's gasps and groans, because the turns run A-B-A-B-A and the vocalization always falls in A's turn 5. A reference carrying two voices lets a cloning renderer pick the wrong one or invent a second; one voice under both tags leaves it nothing to get wrong.
clone_source.tag_numbering_differs_from_the_two_speak: In THIS file S1 is speaker A. In ElevenLabs_ref.mp3 S1 is speaker B and S2 is A. The numbering is per-file and does not carry over — reading 'S1' without checking which file it came from gets it backwards. The first line here is verbatim what A says in the two-speaker clip, which is how the voice was identified.
